description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

scenarios.scenario: A lead data scientist wants to create a new skill from scratch to standardize company-wide pandas data cleaning workflows across their team.
scenarios.user_query: I want to create a new skill called pandas-cleaner that enforces our team's dataframe cleaning standards, handles missing values consistently, and outputs type-annotated code.

scenarios.scenario: A marketing manager just completed an extensive multi-step ad copy generation process in the chat and wants Claude to save the exact workflow for future use.
scenarios.user_query: The way you just broke down our buyer personas, tone matrix, and 3-variant copy structure was fantastic. Can you turn this whole workflow into something permanent so I don't have to explain the setup every time?

scenarios.scenario: An AI platform engineer notices Claude rarely triggers their existing SQL optimizer skill unless directly named, and wants to optimize the frontmatter description.
scenarios.user_query: Our sql-optimizer skill has an undertriggering problem. Can we run the description optimization loop to generate trigger evals and find a description that activates more reliably?

scenarios.scenario: A legal operations specialist has finalized a contract review folder and needs to bundle it into an installable package file.
scenarios.user_query: The contract-reviewer directory in my workspace has all the scripts and references ready. Please package it up into a .skill file so I can distribute it to our legal team.

scenarios.scenario: A software engineer made major prompt changes to an internal code review assistant and wants to test if the new version actually outperforms the baseline across sample pull requests.
scenarios.user_query: I revised the prompt instructions in my code reviewer project. Can you spin up parallel test runs on 3 sample PRs—one using my new instructions and one baseline without them—and let me see the side-by-side results?

scenarios.scenario: A product manager is experiencing formatting regressions in an existing JIRA ticket formatting skill and wants to iteratively fix it with test cases.
scenarios.user_query: Let's edit the jira-ticket-formatter skill. It keeps omitting acceptance criteria tables. Let's write a couple of test cases, run them, and inspect what's failing.

scenarios.scenario: A bioinformatician wants to turn their complex genomic annotation workflow, shell scripts, and reference documentation into a structured agent capability with progressive disclosure.
scenarios.user_query: I have three python scripts for VCF filtering, a markdown guide on clinical significance tiers, and standard output templates. I want to bundle all of this together into a cohesive capability folder where the agent reads the main workflow first and pulls the reference docs only when needed.

scenarios.scenario: A frontend developer is frustrated that Claude ignores their custom Tailwind styling configuration during general UI component generation requests.
scenarios.user_query: I have instructions set up for our design system in tailwind-styler, but whenever I ask 'make a user profile card component', you just use vanilla CSS instead of picking up my styling rules. How do we fix when this gets triggered?

scenarios.scenario: A sales engineer wants to benchmark the execution time, token consumption, and assertion pass rate of their pitch deck creation skill.
scenarios.user_query: Please run a benchmark for pitch-deck-builder against the baseline across our 4 test scenarios in evals.json and aggregate the pass rates, time, and token deltas into benchmark.md.

scenarios.scenario: An operations manager wants an unbiased evaluation between two competing prompt variations of their incident postmortem skill.
scenarios.user_query: I have two versions of the incident-reporter skill in iteration-1 and iteration-2. Can we run a blind comparison with an independent judge agent to determine which output is structured better?

scenarios.scenario: A technical documentation lead wants to create an automated agent tool that checks and rewrites engineering docs according to the Google developer documentation style guide.
scenarios.user_query: I want to build a reusable capability for Claude to audit our markdown documentation against our internal style guide, catch passive voice, fix heading hierarchy, and output diffs.

scenarios.scenario: A DevOps engineer ran test iterations for a Kubernetes diagnostic skill and wants to open the review interface to inspect the outputs.
scenarios.user_query: I just ran test cases for k8s-debugger. Can you run the eval viewer script so I can look at the generated diagnostic reports in my browser and leave feedback on each eval?

scenarios.scenario: A recruiting coordinator had Claude screen 5 candidate resumes using custom scoring rubrics and wants to preserve the exact logic for upcoming hiring rounds.
scenarios.user_query: This resume scoring logic with the 4-tier rubric worked flawlessly on those engineering candidates. I need this to become a standard tool I can invoke for all future interview batches. Can we set that up?

scenarios.scenario: An AI researcher wants to run description optimization on their financial analysis skill using the claude CLI background loop.
scenarios.user_query: Let's generate 20 trigger eval queries for financial-analyst—half positive and half near-misses—and run run_loop.py to train a higher-accuracy skill description.

scenarios.scenario: A customer support lead has an instruction file that grew to over 900 lines, causing the model to get confused and hallucinate policy rules.
scenarios.user_query: My support-policy agent instructions have ballooned into a huge 900-line markdown file and the model keeps missing edge case rules. Can you help me reorganize it into a lean top-level file with modular reference files and scripts?

scenarios.scenario: A security analyst needs to define quantitative assertions for their vulnerability scanning skill test cases.
scenarios.user_query: Let's draft the evals/evals.json for cve-summarizer. I need assertions checking whether CVSS scores are extracted, remediation steps are present, and output is strictly valid JSON.

scenarios.scenario: A real estate analyst notices their valuation prompt produces inconsistent cap rates and wants to see why the model is struggling across test runs.
scenarios.user_query: When I run test properties through my commercial-appraisal workflow, the net operating income numbers are all over the place. Can you inspect the execution transcripts from the test runs and see if we need to bundle a deterministic calculation script?

scenarios.scenario: A video game narrative designer wants to package their dialog branching skill folder into a distributable archive for colleagues.
scenarios.user_query: We finished testing dialogue-tree-builder. Run package_skill.py on the folder so I get the .skill file ready to share with our narrative writers.

scenarios.scenario: A financial analyst wants to build a new skill from the ground up for extracting 10-K filing metrics into standardized financial models.
scenarios.user_query: I want to build a brand new skill called sec-10k-extractor. Let's interview me on the requirements, write the initial SKILL.md, and create a couple of test cases from real quarterly filings.

scenarios.scenario: A research assistant created an academic literature synthesis guide but Claude never uses it when asked to summarize papers.
scenarios.user_query: I created a custom folder of instructions for synthesizing medical journal papers, but whenever I ask you 'summarize this trial paper', you give a standard generic summary instead of using my framework. Why is it being ignored and how do we fix the triggering?

scenarios.scenario: A QA automation engineer wants to aggregate the grading and timing results of their test generator skill after three rounds of prompt tuning.
scenarios.user_query: Run aggregate_benchmark on the workspace iteration-3 directory for cypress-gen so we can compare pass rates and token duration against iteration-1 and iteration-2.

scenarios.scenario: A growth marketing specialist spent two hours troubleshooting an SEO keyword clustering script and wants to convert the finished process into an agent capability.
scenarios.user_query: We finally have the exact step-by-step logic for scraping SERP results, extracting search intent, and grouping keywords into clusters. Capture this entire procedure into a permanent, reusable setup for our workspace.

scenarios.scenario: A solutions architect wants to run an analyzer agent to understand why a competitor's prompt structure outperformed their AWS migration skill.
scenarios.user_query: The blind comparison picked version B as the winner for our aws-migrator eval. Can you run the post-hoc analyzer on both transcripts to tell me specifically what instructions made B succeed where A failed?

scenarios.scenario: A newsletter editor wants to grade their automated layout generator against three sample markdown articles to verify formatting compliance.
scenarios.user_query: Here are three sample newsletter drafts. I want you to run them through our publication formatting guidelines, check if headers, callout boxes, and sponsor disclaimers match our checklist, and give me a grading report of what passed and failed.

scenarios.scenario: A data engineer wants to update an installed skill in a read-only directory without changing its registered name.
scenarios.user_query: I need to update the installed skill etl-pipeline-helper. Please stage it in /tmp/etl-pipeline-helper, keep the exact same skill name frontmatter, apply the new spark SQL guidelines, and package it back up.

scenarios.scenario: A customer success manager finds that their email response assistant frequently hallucinates refund escalation tiers and needs to refine the rules.
scenarios.user_query: Our support email triage assistant is still promising 100% refunds on enterprise tiers when it shouldn't. Let's edit the guidelines to explain why strict policy bounds matter and rerun our standard test cases to verify the fix.

scenarios.scenario: A machine learning engineer wants to generate positive and negative test prompts to optimize triggering for a PyTorch debugging skill.
scenarios.user_query: Let's create the eval query set for pytorch-debugger. Generate 10 realistic queries that should trigger it and 10 tricky negative near-misses that involve Python debugging but shouldn't trigger PyTorch specifics.

scenarios.scenario: A management consultant wants to turn their proprietary pitch deck audit methodology into an agent capability with bundled checklists and scoring scripts.
scenarios.user_query: I have a proprietary 15-point pitch deck assessment methodology that uses a scoring spreadsheet and specific slide layout criteria. I want to build this into a structured AI workflow with all assets and instructions bundled together.

scenarios.scenario: A systems administrator wants to measure the token overhead and accuracy improvement of their server log analysis skill compared to vanilla Claude.
scenarios.user_query: Run a baseline benchmark for sysadmin-log-parser against raw Claude on 5 corrupted nginx log files. I want to see if the skill's regex scripts actually justify the extra token usage.

scenarios.scenario: An executive assistant wants to fix their meeting summarizer instructions because action items are missing due dates in half the test runs.
scenarios.user_query: My meeting-notes assistant keeps dropping due dates and owners from the action items list. Can we set up a few test transcripts, run an evaluation loop, and refine the prompt until it reliably extracts all assignment metadata?
